\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Fourier One-Norm]
\lean{FABL.fourierOneNorm}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p086-b014,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p087-b002
}
\label{FABL.fourierOneNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff}
For a natural number $n$ and a real-valued function $f$ on the sign cube $\\{−1,1\\}^n$,
its Fourier one-norm is the sum, over all subsets $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, of the
absolute values of its Fourier coefficients: $\\sum_{S\\subseteq[n]} |\\widehat f(S)|$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the Fourier one-norm]
\lean{FABL.fourierOneNorm_nonneg}
\label{FABL.fourierOneNorm_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierOneNorm}
\difficulty{2}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, its Fourier one-norm is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm and spectral one norm]
\lean{FABL.fourierOneNorm_eq_spectralPNorm_one}
\label{FABL.fourierOneNorm_eq_spectralPNorm_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.spectralPNorm, FABL.spectralPNorm_one_eq_sum_abs, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. The Fourier one norm of $f$
equals the spectral $1$-norm of the function on $(\mathbb F_2)^n$ obtained by composing
$f$ with the coordinatewise map from bits to signs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Concentrating Fourier Family]
\lean{FABL.l1ConcentratingFourierFamily}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p079-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p087-b002
}
\label{FABL.l1ConcentratingFourierFamily}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm}
For a natural number $n$, a real-valued function $f$ on the sign cube $\\{−1,1\\}^n$,
and a real number $\\varepsilon$, the concentrating Fourier family consists of those
subsets $S\\subseteq[n]$ for which $\\varepsilon\\leq \\|\\widehat f\\|_1 |\\widehat
f(S)|$, where $\\|\\widehat f\\|_1$ is the sum of the absolute values of all Fourier
coefficients of $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the concentrating Fourier family]
\lean{FABL.mem_l1ConcentratingFourierFamily}
\label{FABL.mem_l1ConcentratingFourierFamily}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.l1ConcentratingFourierFamily}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
Boolean cube, let $\\varepsilon\\in\\mathbb{R}$, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates.
Then $S$ belongs to the family concentrating the Fourier coefficients of $f$ in the
$1$-norm if and only if $\\varepsilon\\le \\|\\widehat f\\|_1\\,|\\widehat f(S)|$, where
$\\|\\widehat f\\|_1$ is the sum of the absolute values of all Fourier coefficients of
$f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size of a concentrating Fourier family]
\lean{FABL.card_l1ConcentratingFourierFamily_le}
\label{FABL.card_l1ConcentratingFourierFamily_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierOneNorm, FABL.fourierOneNorm_nonneg, FABL.l1ConcentratingFourierFamily, FABL.mem_l1ConcentratingFourierFamily}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let
$\varepsilon>0$. The number of subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for which
$\varepsilon\leq \|\widehat f\|_1\,|\widehat f(S)|$ is at most $\|\widehat
f\|_1^2/\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product of uniform distributions]
\lean{FABL.uniformPMF_bind_map_pair}
\label{FABL.uniformPMF_bind_map_pair}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite nonempty sets. If $a$ is chosen uniformly from
$\alpha$ and then $b$ independently and uniformly from $\beta$, the resulting
distribution of $(a,b)$ is the uniform distribution on $\alpha\times\beta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Three independent uniform samples]
\lean{FABL.uniformPMF_bind_bind_map_triple}
\label{FABL.uniformPMF_bind_bind_map_triple}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformPMF_bind_map_pair}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite nonempty set. If three elements are sampled independently and
uniformly from $\alpha$, their joint distribution is the uniform distribution on
$\alpha\times\alpha\times\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier Weight]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.liftFixedFrequency, FABL.liftFreeFrequency}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\\{−1,1\\}^n$, let
$J\\subseteq[n]$, and let $S\\subseteq J$. The restricted Fourier weight at $S$ is the
sum, over all subsets $T$ of the coordinates outside $J$, of the squares of the Fourier
coefficients of $f$ indexed by the union of $S$ and $T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of restricted Fourier weight]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight_nonneg}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J$ be a finite set of coordinates, and let $S$ be a finite subset of
$J$. The restricted Fourier weight of $f$ on $J$ at $S$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restricted weight as a mean square]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight_eq_expect_sq_restrictionFourierCoeff}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p077-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b003
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeight_eq_expect_sq_restrictionFourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.expect_sq_restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J$ be a finite set of coordinates, and let $S$ be a finite subset of
$J$. The restricted Fourier weight of $f$ on $J$ at $S$ equals the uniform expectation,
over sign assignments to the coordinates outside $J$, of the square of the corresponding
Fourier coefficient of the restriction of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restriction Coefficient Observation]
\lean{FABL.restrictionCoefficientObservation}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p076-b001}
\label{FABL.restrictionCoefficientObservation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.indexedMonomial}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\\{−1,1\\}^n$, and
let $J\\subseteq[n]$ and $S\\subseteq J$. Fix signs $z$ on the coordinates outside $J$
and signs $y$ on $J$. The restriction coefficient observation is the value of $f$ on the
combined sign assignment, multiplied by the character indexed by $S$ evaluated at $y$.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.restrictionCoefficientObservation}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p076-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p075-b004}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
let $S\subseteq J$, and fix a sign assignment $z$ outside $J$. The mean, over a uniform
sign assignment $Y$ on $J$, of $f$ evaluated at the combined assignment $(Y,z)$ times
the monomial $\chi_S(Y)$ equals the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the restriction of $f$
obtained by fixing the outside coordinates to $z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier Weight Observation]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b003
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.restrictionCoefficientObservation}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\\{−1,1\\}^n$, and
let $J\\subseteq[n]$ and $S\\subseteq J$. Fix signs $z$ outside $J$ and signs $y,y'$ on
$J$. The restricted Fourier weight observation is the product of the restriction
coefficient observations at $y$ and at $y'$, using the same $f,J,S,z$.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be
a finite set, let $S\subseteq J$, and fix a sign assignment $z$ on the coordinates
outside $J$. If $Y,Y'$ are independent uniform sign assignments on $J$, then the
expected product of $f$ evaluated at the combined assignments $(Y,z)$ and $(Y',z)$,
multiplied by the corresponding monomial $\chi_S(Y)\chi_S(Y')$, equals the square of the
Fourier coefficient of the restriction of $f$ at $S$ with outside assignment $z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restricted Fourier weight identity]
\lean{FABL.expect_restrictedFourierWeightObservation_eq_restrictedFourierWeight}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005
}
\label{FABL.expect_restrictedFourierWeightObservation_eq_restrictedFourierWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.expect_restrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight_eq_expect_sq_restrictionFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
and let $S\subseteq J$. If $Z$ is a uniform sign assignment outside $J$ and $Y,Y'$ are
independent uniform sign assignments on $J$, then the expected restricted Fourier weight
observation is the restricted Fourier weight of $f$ at $J,S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Square of an indexed sign monomial]
\lean{FABL.indexedMonomial_sq}
\label{FABL.indexedMonomial_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one}
\difficulty{4}
For any index type, any finite set $S$ of indices, and any sign assignment $x$, the
square of the real monomial on $S$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds on a restricted Fourier observation]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.indexedMonomial_sq, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.restrictionCoefficientObservation, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J$ be a finite set of coordinates in $br^n$, and let
$S$ be a finite subset of $J$. For every Boolean target function, every assignment of
signs to the coordinates outside $J$, and every two assignments of signs to the
coordinates in $J$, the restricted Fourier weight observation lies in $[-1,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Rational restricted Fourier weight observation]
\lean{FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation}
\label{FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.Sign, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.rationalFourierObservation}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $J$ be a finite set of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates,
let $S\subseteq J$, let $z$ assign a sign to each coordinate outside $J$, and let $y,y'$
assign signs to coordinates in $J$. For signs $a,a'$, the rational restricted Fourier
weight observation is the product of the rational Fourier observation at the lifted
frequency determined by $S$ for the combined inputs $(y,z)$ and output $a$, and the
corresponding observation for $(y',z)$ and output $a'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Casting the restricted weight observation]
\lean{FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation_cast}
\label{FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.fourierObservation, FABL.rationalFourierObservation_cast, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.restrictionCoefficientObservation}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $S\subseteq J$. For any fixed sign
assignment $z$ on the coordinates outside $J$ and any two sign assignments $y,y'$ on
$J$, the rational observation formed from the labels $f(y,z)$ and $f(y',z)$ and their
respective lifted Fourier observations, regarded as a real number, equals the product of
the two corresponding real restricted Fourier coefficient observations.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier weight observation from full inputs]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n$ coordinates, let $J$ be a
finite set of those coordinates, and let $S\subseteq J$. Given three full sign vectors
$z,y,y'\in\{\pm1\}^n$, split each into its coordinates in $J$ and outside $J$. The
restricted Fourier weight observation from these inputs is the restricted Fourier weight
observation for $f$, $J$, and $S$, evaluated using the outside-$J$ part of $z$ and the
inside-$J$ parts of $y$ and $y'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rational observation from full inputs]
\lean{FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs}
\label{FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n$ coordinates, let $J$ be a
finite subset of those coordinates, and let $S\subseteq J$. For full sign vectors
$z,y,y'\in\{\pm1\}^n$, split each into its outside-$J$ and inside-$J$ parts, denoting
these by $z_0,y_0,y'_0$ and $z_1,y_1,y'_1$, respectively. The rational observation is
the rational restricted Fourier weight observation at $J,S,z_0,y_1,y'_1$, with the two
output signs given by $f$ evaluated at the combined inputs $(y_1,z_0)$ and $(y'_1,z_0)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Casting the restricted weight observation from inputs]
\lean{FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs_cast}
\label{FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation_cast, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $S\subseteq J$. For any three
sign-cube inputs, use the first input's coordinates outside $J$ as a fixed assignment
and the second and third inputs' coordinates in $J$ as free assignments $y$ and $y'$.
The rational observation formed from the two labels $f(y,z)$ and $f(y',z)$ and their
respective lifted Fourier observations, when viewed as a real number, equals the product
of the two corresponding real restricted Fourier coefficient observations.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average of a fixed-coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.expect_fixedProjection_signCubeSplitEquiv}
\label{FABL.expect_fixedProjection_signCubeSplitEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
\difficulty{4}
Let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and let $g$ be a real-valued function of sign assignments
on the complement of $J$. If $x$ is uniform on $\{-1,1\}^n$, then the average of $g$
applied to the restriction of $x$ to that complement equals the uniform average of $g$
over all sign assignments on the complement.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform free-coordinate projection]
\lean{FABL.expect_freeProjection_signCubeSplitEquiv}
\label{FABL.expect_freeProjection_signCubeSplitEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
\difficulty{4}
Let $J$ be a subset of the coordinate indices $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, and let $g$ be any
real-valued function on sign assignments to $J$. Under a uniformly random sign
assignment to all $n$ coordinates, the restriction to $J$ is uniform; consequently, the
expected value of $g$ on that restriction equals the uniform expectation of $g$ over
assignments to $J$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $F:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
and let $S\subseteq J$. For three independent uniformly distributed full sign vectors
$Z,Y,Y'\in\{−1,1\}^n$, split $Z$ into its coordinates outside $J$, and split each of
$Y,Y'$ into its coordinates in $J$. The expected restricted Fourier weight observation
formed from these pieces and the real-valued sign function associated to $F$ equals the
restricted Fourier weight of that real-valued function at $J,S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds on an input-derived observation]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservation_mem_Icc, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J$ be a finite set of coordinates in $br^n$, and let
$S$ be a finite subset of $J$. For every Boolean target function and every three inputs
in the $n$-dimensional sign cube, the restricted Fourier weight observation formed from
these inputs lies in $[-1,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Equivalence between batches and sample triples]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightBatchEquiv}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightBatchEquiv}
\leanok
For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, there is a bijection between triples of batches, each
batch consisting of $m$ sign vectors on $n$ coordinates, and a batch of $m$ triples of
sign vectors on $n$ coordinates. The bijection pairs entries with the same index, and
its inverse separates each indexed triple into its three coordinate batches.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier weight triple observation]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightTripleObservation}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightTripleObservation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n$ coordinates, let $J$ be a
finite subset of those coordinates, and let $S\subseteq J$. For an ordered triple of
full sign vectors $(z,y,y')\in(\{\pm1\}^n)^3$, the restricted Fourier weight triple
observation is the restricted Fourier weight observation obtained from $f,J,S$ and the
three inputs $z,y,y'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Triple-input restricted Fourier weight identity]
\lean{FABL.expect_restrictedFourierWeightTripleObservation}
\label{FABL.expect_restrictedFourierWeightTripleObservation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.expect_restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs_eq_restrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightTripleObservation}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $F:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
and let $S\subseteq J$. For three independent uniform full sign vectors, the expected
triple-input restricted Fourier weight observation equals the restricted Fourier weight
of the real-valued sign function associated to $F$ at $J,S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Empirical restricted Fourier weight concentration]
\lean{FABL.measure_restrictedFourierWeightTripleEmpiricalMean_failure_le}
\label{FABL.measure_restrictedFourierWeightTripleEmpiricalMean_failure_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.expect_restrictedFourierWeightTripleObservation, FABL.finiteUniformEmpiricalMean, FABL.measure_finiteUniformEmpiricalMean_sub_expect_ge_le, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs_mem_Icc, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightTripleObservation, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, let
$J\subseteq[n]$, and let $S\subseteq J$. For each triple of cube inputs, split each
input into its coordinates in $J$ and outside $J$, use the outside coordinates of the
first input as a fixed assignment, and use the $J$-coordinates of the second and third
inputs as two free assignments; let the observation be the product of the two values of
$f$ at the resulting cube points, each multiplied by the monomial on $S$ of its free
assignment. If $m>0$ independent uniform triples are sampled and their observations are
averaged, then for every $\varepsilon\ge 0$, the probability that this average differs
from the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ over frequencies formed by adjoining
any outside-$J$ frequency to $S$ by at least $\varepsilon$ is at most
$2\exp(-m\varepsilon^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}
